scope: Theorem 5.2 (Distributed density compression) of the manuscript “Polynomial PEPS approximation of gapped square-grid ground states” (preprints/Polynomial-PEPS-approximation-of-gapped-square-grid-ground-states-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 265 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 0b55ba0b87ad0468), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 27-28. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Consider a family of distributed constructions indexed by L ≥ 2 with the following uniform properties. 1. The number of parties and gates is uniformly polynomial. The initial vector is a tensor product of normalized private vectors, one at each party, and every gate is a contraction. 2. There is a constant b such that each nonprivate gate involves at most b parties, and each party participates in at most b nonprivate gates over the entire construction. 3. Each nonprivate gate is a sum of uniformly polynomially many allowed monomials with uniformly polynomially bounded scalar coefficients. There is a constant r bounding the number of pair sources, pair effects, and polynomial-dimensional messages in each monomial. All constituent local maps are contractions. 4. At the end, the intended physical output space of each party has uniformly polynomial dimension. All other registers are traced out party by party. Write ρ for the resulting physical output density operator; it is positive and may have trace less than one. For every fixed p > 0, there is an operator tensor network σ satisfying ∥σ − ρ∥1 ≤ L−p . It has one node per party, a bounded number of incident virtual links at each node, and uniformly polynomial link dimensions. Every link joins two parties which participate in a common nonprivate gate of the original construction. The physical legs at a node are the ket and bra legs of that party’s intended output. The constants in these bounds depend only on p and the fixed uniform data in the assumptions, including b, r and the polynomial bounds, and not on private dimensions or source Schmidt ranks. 27 The same conclusion holds if the gate expansions in the third assumption are available to every fixed inverse-polynomial operator-norm accuracy, with uniform polynomial bounds at each fixed accuracy.
